title: Elastic priority credits + region-aware admission shedder with graceful rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Implement an adaptive load-shedding component that uses per-tenant elastic priority credits and region-aware admission thresholds to keep latency SLOs intact during spikes and multi-region failover. The component must (1) prioritize critical tenant lanes, (2) allow soft degradation modes instead of hard rejects, and (3) support instant rollback to conservative defaults if a release causes correctness regressions. This ticket covers design, prototype, automated tests, and a limited canary rollout to EU and us-west regions.
design_summary: We will extend the admission controller with an Elastic Priority Credits (EPC) layer. Each tenant is assigned priority bands (critical, standard, best-effort). Instead of fixed token buckets per band, EPC grants time-windowed credits that replenish based on historical SLO consumption and recent success rates. Region-aware multipliers adjust credits for deployments that have degraded inter-region capacity. On admission, requests consume credits; when credits are low, the controller falls back to a graceful degradation policy: (a) response-slimming (truncate nonessential tokens), (b) model-variant skewing (route to lower-cost/fast variant), (c) deferred-execution reservoir (queue low-priority requests with guaranteed retry windows). A safe rollback mechanism — the Rollback Token Reservoir (RTR) — tracks admission changes and can revert to conservative bucket parameters within a single fleet cycle if error budgets spike.
acceptance_criteria: Canary in eu-central-1 and us-west-2 with traffic shaping: no more than 5% SLO breach increase for P99 latency compared to baseline
Graceful degradations (slim, variant, reservoir) triggered under load and observable in Console dashboards
Automated chaos test where primary region fails and EPC multipliers adapt to secondary region without major SLA regressions
Runbook entries and Grafana panels added; on-call can flip rollout and trigger RTR within 2 minutes
implementation_notes: Key components: EPC service (lightweight controller kept near gateways), admission plugin for runtime frontends, degradation strategy registry, RTR state stored in etcd with limited retention. Admission decisions must be idempotent and cheap (sub-microsecond path). We'll expose per-tenant credit metadata in tracing and the Console. Use existing token-bucket library but wrap with time-windowed replenishment and multiplier hooks for region health metrics.
testing_plan: Unit tests for EPC replenishment math, integration tests for admission plugin, load tests using rps-multi-region harness (scripts in github.com/redwood-inference/load-tests/tree/epc), and failure injection scenario in staging cluster simulating zone and region failovers. We'll add end-to-end acceptance that asserts request fidelity metrics under degradation.
monitoring_and_alerting: New Grafana panels: EPC usage by tenant, credits-per-band, degradation-mode-trigger-rate, RTR-rollback-events. Alerts: credit-depletion-rate > 0.8 for 5m, rollback-triggered more than twice in 1h, canary-slo-delta > 5%. Instrumentation PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/784
progress_updates: 2025-01-15: Architecture review with infra and runtime teams — agreed to colocate EPC control path with gateway proxies to reduce decision latency
2025-01-27: Prototype EPC replenishment algorithm implemented (simulation harness shows improved P99 retention in synthetic tenant mix)
2025-02-04: Integration branch created and initial admission plugin wired into canary agents (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2563)
2025-02-12: Load tests against staging with 3x normal traffic — graceful degradation paths exercised; observed 12% reduction in hard rejects compared to token-bucket baseline
2025-02-19: Design review notes applied; added RTR guardrails and conservative defaults; preparing canary rollout plan
review_feedback: Infra: Ensure EPC control plane is horizontally scalable; add p95 decision latency metric
Security: Confirm that per-tenant metadata exposed in traces is scrubbed of PII
Runtime: Admission path must be lock-free; use atomic compare-and-swap for credit adjustments
PM: Add acceptance that customer-facing error messages remain unchanged during degradation
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Miscalibrated multipliers could starve regions during failover. Mitigation: start with conservative multipliers and gradually increase via canary with traffic shaping
Risk: Increased decision latency impacting P50. Mitigation: colocate EPC with gateways and keep hot-path logic lock-free
Risk: Unexpected correctness regressions when routing to model variants. Mitigation: require model-compatibility tags and add fast rollback hooks (RTR)
next_steps: Execute small canary (1% traffic) in eu-central-1 on 2025-02-25
Run chaos experiment: simulate us-west-2 AZ outage and validate EPC multiplier adjustments and RTR behavior
Post-mortem template prepared to capture canary learnings and adjust replenishment curve
